# CLAUDE.md

Ranks South Dakota high school cross country runners from meet results. Written in R. The owner is a statistician; keep code plain and easy to read.

## How it works

Every run rescores the whole season from the curated files. There is no saved state, so late results only need adding and a rerun.

```
convert.r   source TXT / saved MileSplit page -> {year}/Data/{meet}_{boys|girls}.csv   (rebuilds all)
run.r       load -> check -> score -> {year}/output/rankings_{boys|girls}.csv (one ranking per week)
export.r    rankings CSVs -> ../sdxc/data/{boys|girls}_{year}_week{N}.json + schools_{year}.json for the website (sister repo)
```

- `R/load.r`: reads the files and applies school and athlete aliases.
- `R/check.r`: data checks. ERRORs stop the run; WARNINGs don't.
- `R/score.r`: scoring and weekly ranking.
- `R/convert.r`: TXT and MileSplit parsers.

Run from the repo root with Windows R: `"/mnt/c/Program Files/R/R-4.5.3/bin/x64/Rscript.exe" run.r`. `/run-sdxc` runs it, fixes what the check reports, then runs export.r.

## Curated files (the owner maintains these)

| File | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `{year}/meet_list.csv` | per year | Every meet: `meet` (file stem), `date`, `week`, `flg_5k`, `missing`, `alternative` (1 = results from the MileSplit URLs in `alternative_boys/girls`) |
| `{year}/schools.csv` | per year | In-state schools, their class (AA/A/B) and region (1A–5A, 1B–5B; blank for AA); classes, regions and co-ops change yearly. Regions come from GoBound's teams page (`gobound.com/sd/sdhsaa/boyscrosscountry/{2026-27}/Teams?sortby=Region`, and girls), checked by hand once per season. |
| `school_aliases.csv` | all years | raw school name -> standard name, `OUT` (out of state) or `DROP` (not a school). Never delete rows. |
| `{year}/athlete_aliases.csv` | per year | `name,school,correct_name` for misspelled runners (school = standardized name) |
| `{year}/different_athletes.csv` | per year | Similar-name pairs confirmed to be different pe

content.text:
Not hard. I'd guess a few hours, and most of the work is on the data side, not the UI.

**Why it's not just a UI change:** the site never gets race-by-race results. Each `data/{gender}_{year}_week{N}.json` file has only the runner's adjusted time, PR, rank and class. The individual results (place, time, meet) live only in `sdxc-data`, in `{year}/Data/*.csv` and `meet_list.csv`.

**What it would take:**

1. **Data export (the main work).** Add a step to `sdxc-data/export.r` that writes one results file per gender and season, e.g. `data/results_boys_2026.json`, with rows like `{ id, meet, date, place, time }`.
   - It has to come from the results after `R/load.r` applies the school and athlete aliases, not from the raw CSVs. Otherwise misspelled names won't match the runner's `id`.
   - The `id` is already the same for a runner all season, so it links straight to the rankings rows.
   - Size is fine: 2026 has about 6,800 result rows, so the file is a few hundred KB.
   - It would be easy to include the meet name, whether it was a 5K (`flg_5k`) and the field size ("4th of 87").
2. **Site:** load that file in `src/data.ts` and add a `RaceResult` type. Then make the runner's name in `RankingsTable.tsx` clickable, so it opens a list under the row: date, meet, place, time. About 50–80 lines.
3. **Things to note:**
   - **2023:** the scoring pipeline doesn't cover it, so it would have no race history unless that data is cleaned up separately.
   - **Mid-season weeks:** if you're viewing an earlier week, the list should probably show only races up to that week. That's a simple filter on the meet's `week`.
   - **Optional extra:** each race's course-adjusted time, which would show why someone is ranked where they are. It would mean also exporting the meet effects from `R/score.r`.

Want me to build it, starting with the `export.r` change?

content.text:
Your summary covered everything I needed, so I built the feature. It type-checks and the production build succeeds. I haven't clicked through it in a browser yet.

**What it does:** on the Rankings tab, each runner's name is now a button with a small down-arrow. Clicking it opens a list right under their row with the date, meet, place ("7th of 64") and time. Races that weren't 5Ks are marked "(not 5K)". The list only shows races up to the week you're viewing. You can open several runners at once to compare them.

**Changes:**
- `src/types.ts`: new `RaceResult` type matching the JSON format.
- `src/data.ts`: `getResults(gender, year)` loads the new results files.
- `src/format.ts`: `ordinal()` turns 7 into "7th".
- `src/components/RankingsTable.tsx`: the clickable name and the race list. For 2023 and 2025 there are no results files, so names stay plain text.

**About Augustana's field of 502:** it looks like one real race. Places run 1–502 with no gaps or restarts, and times go steadily from 14:53 to 27:35 across 89 schools. Augie Twilight is known for a huge open field, so "3rd of 502" is probably right. Only the meet's own program can confirm it.

**Before it goes live:**
- **Push the data files.** `results_boys_2026.json` and `results_girls_2026.json` aren't committed yet. The live site reads data from GitHub, so the feature won't work there until they're pushed.
- **Commit `export.r` in sdxc-data.** It's changed but not committed.
- **Use Windows npm to build.** Your `node_modules` was installed from Windows, so building from WSL fails on esbuild. `cmd.exe /c "npm run build"` works.

content.content:
# Build and deploy to GitHub Pages. Every push to master that touches the
# app builds it; the deploy is blocked unless the type check and build
# pass. Pull requests run the build only.
#
# Data pushes (data/**) don't redeploy: the site fetches rankings, schools
# and manifest.json live from raw.githubusercontent.com at runtime, so new
# weeks from sdxc-data's export.r go live as soon as they're pushed.
name: Build and deploy

on:
  push:
    branches: [master]
    paths-ignore: ["data/**", "**.md"]
  pull_request:
    paths-ignore: ["data/**", "**.md"]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm

      # npm ci installs exactly package-lock.json, including the Linux
      # esbuild binary that a Windows-side node_modules lacks
      - run: npm ci

      # build = tsc --noEmit && vite build, so type errors block the deploy
      - run: npm run build

      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        with:
          path: dist

  deploy:
    needs: build
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      pages: write
      id-token: write
    concurrency:
      group: pages
      cancel-in-progress: true
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

content.text:
Yes, they do, so you don't need to build locally to deploy. `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` runs `npm ci` and then `npm run build` on every push to master that changes the app. If the type check or build fails, nothing deploys. I shouldn't have listed the Windows npm build as a step before going live. It only matters if you want to test the build on your own machine, and I did that just to check my changes.

What the workflow does mean for this feature:
- **Code and data deploy differently.** Changes under `data/**` don't trigger a deploy, because the live site fetches data straight from GitHub.
- **One push covers both.** If you commit the code change and the two `results_*.json` files together, the code change triggers a deploy and the data is live as soon as the push lands.
- **Order matters if you push separately.** If the code goes first, the names stay plain text until the data arrives, because names only become clickable when the results file loads. Nothing breaks either way.
